failure.observation: Failure while acquiring four listeners, before the test had made any FTP data connection; failed before NFS regression started.

diagnosis: Fixture selected passive ports adjacent to an OS-assigned ephemeral control port and released the probes before control/API/TLS connections. These ports can subsequently be allocated as client source ports. This is a plausible collision path inferred from code; the failing runner did not retain a socket table.
change: Probe four random ports in 20000..29999, outside default Windows/Linux ephemeral client ranges; keep production four-port capacity and exhaustion assertions unchanged.

checks: M3 state adds isolated FTP worker; plaintext default deny, anonymous/active/FXP/downgrade denied
stdlib FTP client: UTF-8, PASV, MLSD/MLST facts, directories/rename/delete, binary roundtrip and safe REST upload/download
EPSV ALL and TLS certificate verification; fresh or different-control TLS sessions rejected on data channel
configured passive port exhaustion returns 425 and releases listeners on ABOR/QUIT
in-band ABOR and missing TLS close_notify discard staging, preserve existing file, release quota
bounded malformed commands, mismatched data peer, stalled TLS, quota overflow and changed-source resume rejection
share revocation during STOR cleans unpublished data; disabled credentials invalidate existing control sessions
FTP kill/restart reclaims stages; API, identity, file and DAV processes survive; mixed writer gate retained
independent curl explicit FTPS probe (strict session binding retained)
bounded streaming upload/download 1 MiB with digest verification
explicit plaintext opt-in works after restart with stdlib and curl; default remains TLS only
